name: Arrábida Bridge
short: The 1963 reinforced-concrete arch bridge by engineer Edgar Cardoso, with a 270-metre span, among the longest concrete arch spans of its time.
long: The Arrábida Bridge was Porto's first major reinforced-concrete arch bridge and an achievement of engineer Edgar Cardoso. Its 270-metre main span was the longest of any concrete arch bridge in the world when it opened. The bridge carries six lanes of traffic between the IC1 motorway in Gaia and Porto's ring road, and its arch rises 52 metres. Since 2016 a walking tour, Porto Bridge Climb, has crossed the arch.
history:
In March 1952 the preliminary design of a road bridge over the Douro was awarded to Professor Edgar António Mesquita Cardoso; the project was approved in 1955. Construction began in May 1957 and was completed in June 1963.

The bridge was Porto's first major reinforced-concrete arch bridge and, when it opened, its 270-metre main span was the longest of any concrete arch bridge in the world. The total length of the deck is 493.2 metres and its width 26.5 metres.

The arch rises 52 metres, and the maximum clearance above the water reaches 70 metres. The bridge carries six traffic lanes and two pedestrian walkways; it links the IC1 motorway in Gaia with Porto's ring road (VCI) and stands downstream of the Dom Luís I Bridge, closest to the mouth of the Douro.

The bridge was inaugurated on 22 June 1963. In the 1990s the lifts in the piers, which descended to the riverside, were deactivated, and on 24 June 2016 the Porto Bridge Climb attraction opened, allowing visitors to climb the arch via 262 steps. In 2013 the bridge was declared a national monument.
facts: Opened on 22 June 1963; Edgar Cardoso's design was approved in 1955.
Its 270 m main span was the world's longest concrete arch span when it opened.
Clearance above the water is 70 m; total length 493.2 m, width 26.5 m.
It carries six traffic lanes and two pedestrian walkways between Porto and Gaia.
Since 2016 the Porto Bridge Climb tour crosses the arch (262 steps).
tip: Head to the viewpoint near the bridge at sunset: the contrast between the concrete arch and Porto's lights is especially photogenic. Climbing the arch requires booking the Porto Bridge Climb in advance.
